translation:
Jivandasji Maharaj says that the God-essence (bhagavat-tattva) is secretly manifest in every body (ghat). The true guru has revealed its mystery — that this one form of God exists in the form of Ramchandra, the lord of Sita (Sitapati).

_ghatghat vyapak jivana | sitapatiko roop ||
guru krupa ta daasku | ja ghat naam swaroop ||122||_ (Pervading every body, O Jivana, is the form of Sitapati [Ram]. By the guru's grace, that devotee attains the Name-form present within every body.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the radiance of this God, Sitapati Ram's form, pervades every body. But it is in the body of that devotee upon whom the guru's grace rests that God dwells in the form of the Name.

_hast mastak aave nahi | ghatghat vyapak ram ||
sadguru samjhayo jivana | je samro sitaram ||140||_ (Ram, who pervades every body, cannot be grasped by hand or by the intellect. The true guru has explained, O Jivana: remember and recite that Sitaram.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: that God who pervades the body of everyone cannot be brought under anyone's control or grasp, nor caught within anyone's intellect. Remember and worship that same Lord Sitaram — this is what the true guru has explained.

_ghatghat vyapak ek | pan preet van pachho osare ||
mukh chave vaans | ikh kaaj tene sare ||92||_ (The One pervades every body alike, but without love it withdraws again — as the mouth chews on bare reed, which does not serve the purpose that sugarcane does.)

_anant kot vaasidado | sakal pakhkaa mool ||
narsandh ghatghat pekhiye | gayaa te sanse sool ||148||_ (Countless tens of millions are but His sweepings; He is the root of every side and party. Behold Narsandh present in every body; for those who have gone to Him, the thorn of doubt is gone. The printed book sets this couplet down on its own between blank lines, with no commentary of its own.)

_nij mool nij naam hai | daasi palowe paay ||
so ghatghat vyapak jivana | brij kul taare gaay ||84||_ (His own root is His own Name; the handmaiden [Lakshmiji] massages His feet in service. That very one, O Jivana, who pervades every body, tends the cows in the Brij clan.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: the God-essence has its own principal seat in His Name. Lakshmiji herself serves at the feet of that God who bears the divine Name; devotees of the dasya-bhava (the disposition of a handmaiden), full of loving devotion, worship Him in that same spirit. Such a God-essence pervades every body, in all that moves and does not move. That God grazes the cows in the pastures of Vraj-mandal.

Adhyaruji Maharaj says in the Harsh Bhavan (chapter):

_jotam janjan joojvo | ane jag sacharachar soy ||
ravi aapope mandine | patra vilane joy ||34||_ (Looking closely, God appears different from person to person, and in this moving and unmoving world too He is that same one appearing in different forms — like the one sun, seen reflected differently when placed before different vessels.)

God appears different to each and every person. And in this world, in all that moves and does not move, He, the very same One, dwells in different forms. Just as when we look at one and the same sun, it appears different in different vessels [of water], so too the Lord, the very same One, dwells in different bodies.

In the Brahmanda Purana, Ram said to Vasishtha:

_yatha anek kumbheshu ravir eko api drushyate |
tatha sarveshu bhooteshu chintaniyo asau sada ||_ (Just as, though there are many pots, the reflection of the one sun appears different in each, so too in all beings the one Supreme Soul appears as though different — this should always be reflected upon.)

Just as, though there are many pots, the reflection of the one sun appears different in each, so too in all bodies, the one and same Supreme Soul appears as though different. This should always be reflected upon.

_udakpatra sahastreshu jyotir eko avabhasate |
tathaik aatma sarvatra vastuto bhaasate vibhuh ||_ (Just as there may be thousands of pots filled with water, but the light of the moon or sun falls equally and alike in all of them, so too the Supreme Soul remains ever radiant, alike, in all beings and things.)

Just as there may be thousands of pots filled with water, but the light of the moon or the sun falls equally the same in all of them, in that same way, the Supreme Soul too remains ever radiant in all living beings and in all things.

An illustration: once, at some place, people of all different sects and opinions were sitting together, arguing among themselves about their differing views. No one was ready to accept anyone else's position, and everyone kept praising his own view. In the end, the quarrel reached the point where sticks were about to be raised. At that point, one of the saints among them spoke up: "Brothers, why are you engaging in this useless argument? Look —"

_ghatghatme hari ek hai | taame nahi vishek ||
jaiso footi aarsi | khand khand mukh ek ||_ (Hari is one alone within every body — in that there is no difference. It is like a broken mirror: in each shard, the same one face is seen.)

Hearing this, everyone spoke as one voice:

_tileshu tailam dadhi niva sarpi | jaranya strotassu aranishu chaagnih |
evam aatma-aatmani sannigruhyate | satyena inam tapasa yo anupashyati ||_ (As oil is in sesame seed, ghee is in curd, water is in a mountain spring, and the flame of fire is in the arani [kindling-wood], so Parbrahma, the Supreme Soul, is present everywhere.)

As oil is in sesame seed, ghee is in curd, water is in a mountain spring, and the flame of fire is in the arani (fire-wood used for kindling), in that same way Parbrahma, the Supreme Soul, is present everywhere.

_sab ghat chhaya ramki | pragat ghat hai daas ||
aur ghatme gop hai | unme bhaya prakash ||_ (The reflection of Ram is in every body; but it is manifest openly in the body of His devotee. In other bodies it remains hidden, though its light is present within them.)

Gnaniji Maharaj says: in all bodies there is a reflection of God, but in the body of the saint (devotee), He is present in manifest form. In other bodies, He remains hidden/secret. Thus His influence pervades the entire world.

_gnani sab ghat antar ram hai | jyon jal madhye aakash |
nishchal jal e nirmala | haale taame naash ||65||_ (Ram is within every body, O wise one — like the sky reflected in water. In water that is still, this [reflection] is clear; when it stirs, it is lost.)

Gnaniji Maharaj says: Ram dwells within, inside every single body. He remains there just as the reflection of the sky remains within water. But in water that is not stirring, that reflection appears clear; and if it stirs, that reflection is lost.

_nishchal jal e daas hai | haale soi jiv ||
gnani gurugaam dekhiya | sadhu janme piv ||69||_ (The still water is the devotee; that which stirs is the jiva [the ordinary soul]. The wise one, having seen through the guru's teaching, knows the Beloved dwells among the saintly.)

Gnaniji Maharaj says: the water that is still/steady represents the saint-devotee, and the water that stirs represents the ordinary jivatma (individual soul). Through this mystery revealed by the guru, it is understood that God dwells within saint-devotees.

_sab ghat bhitar me basu | mohi milai na koy ||
jo kachhu karu so mai karu | naam bandeka hoy ||5||_ (I dwell within every body, yet none finds Me. Whatever I do, I alone do it, but it is the servant's name that is spoken as the doer.)

Das Kabirji says, in the Aap Alekh Anga (chapter): "I (God) dwell within every body, yet no one finds Me. Whatever I do, I alone do it, but the doer's name that gets spoken is that of the devoted servant."

_sab ghat bhitar me khara (ram hai) | esa aap sujaan |
aape aapso bandhiya | aape bhaya ajaan ||_ (Within every body dwells the True One [Ram] — know this for yourself with certainty. You yourself have bound yourself, and you yourself have become the ignorant one.)

Das Kabirji says: be certain, in this way, that God truly resides within every body. It is by your own mind that you become bound in bondage; it appears that you have fallen into bondage without having understood this mystery.

_mai manme jaana huta | aur na tha ko paas ||
to sab ghat bhitar ko lahu | sab ghat mero vaas ||8||_ (I knew, within my own mind, one hidden thing — that there was no one else beside Me. So then whom should I take to be within every body? For every body is my own dwelling.)

Das Kabirji says God speaks thus: "I knew, within my own mind, a hidden secret — that there was no one else beside Me. So then, whom should I take to be within all these bodies? For it is I Myself who dwell within every single body."

_mujsa sabko dekhiye | par muj sarikha nahi koy ||
muj jaisa manme rahai | nahi na dekho doy ||7||_ (Everyone will appear like Me, yet none is truly My equal; but if the same disposition as Mine dwells within one's mind, then nothing but Myself will be seen.)

Das Kabirji says: everyone will appear to be like Me, but there will be no one equal to Me; yet if the same disposition as Mine remains within one's mind, then no other besides Myself will be perceived.

_ish eko avagantavyo | naana mata nivishtakaih |
bhinne kache yatha murtir | bhidyate vastuto aprithak ||_ (This one Ishwar is to be known as present everywhere alike by people of every differing doctrine — just as in a broken mirror the reflected face appears in many separate pieces, though in truth it remains one.)

People holding different kinds of doctrines/opinions ought to know that this one Ishwar (God) is present everywhere as one alone — just as in a broken mirror the face appears in many separate pieces, yet in truth it is one.

_sab hi ghatme hari base | jyon girisutme jyoti |
gnan guru manme rahai | nahi na dekho doy ||7||_ (Hari dwells within every single body, as light dwells within the mountain's daughter [i.e., pervading it through and through]. When the guru's knowledge abides in the mind, nothing but that One is seen.)

Das Kabirji says: God dwells in every single body. Just as sparks of fire do not come out of a flint stone unless it is struck against iron, in that same way, without a guru who gives us understanding, the God present within us cannot be made manifest.

Aiming at those followers of the path of knowledge (jnana-marg) who, by recognizing the God present in every body as the Supreme Soul, wish to declare themselves as Brahma — it is true that, since Parmeshwar is present in every body, there is a principle by which one is a form of Brahma, but only as a fragment/portion of the Complete Brahma (Purna Brahma); yet these Brahma-jnanis (self-styled knowers of Brahma) force upon everyone the claim that they themselves are the Complete Brahma in full. Therefore Kabirji, in the Kaami Anga (chapter), has exposed and censured them.

_kabir gnani to nidhadak bhaya | mane nahi shank ||
indri kere bas pare | bhugate vishaye nihshank ||36||_ (Kabir says: these men of knowledge have become so bold that they hold no shame; fallen under the sway of the senses, they indulge in sensory pleasures without any hesitation.)

Das Kabirji says: these so-called men of knowledge have become so bold and shameless that they keep no shame of any kind — they have become subject to their senses, and without any doubt, fear, or hesitation, they indulge in sensory pleasures.

_kabir gnani mool gamaiya | aape bhaya kartar ||
tathe to sansari bhula | manme rahe darta ||37||_ (Kabir says: these men of knowledge have lost their very roots, having come to believe themselves the Doer. Compared to them, worldly people, mistaken as they are, at least remain fearful [and restrained] in their minds.)

Das Kabirji says: these men of knowledge have abandoned every trace of shame and propriety from the very root, and have come to believe as if they themselves have become the Doer, the "I am Brahma" Supreme Being. Compared to them, ordinary worldly people are better — for they, keeping worldly shame and propriety, live fearfully within the bounds of honor and restraint.

_kabir bhagati bigadi bhudeve | kathi kathi brahmagyan ||
gatrandaki sundari | kyon pave santan ||39||_ (Kabir says: the earth-gods [the Brahmins] have ruined devotion by preaching, again and again, the talk of Brahma-knowledge. How can the wife of an impotent man ever obtain a child?)

Das Kabirji says: those called "gods on earth" — the Brahmins — by preaching, again and again, the talk of Brahma-jnana (knowledge of Brahma), have ruined loving devotion (prem-bhakti). Just as the wife of an impotent man cannot obtain a child, in the same way, how can such feeble followers of Brahma-jnana ever attain true devotion?

(Raga Ashavari)

_santo sab hi ved kul mahi | tathe rogi jive nahi ||tek||
kahe harie gopi khandhe lidhi | aisi bhagati dradhave ||
jaisi sune taisi man upaje | tam lahar vikhki aave ||1||
gnan kathi gnan dradhave | trigun nadime bore ||
brahmagyaniku kahu thaur nahi | ya vidh bhagati na hoy re ||2||
puran brahma davanal pidho | giri govardhan dhari |
sol sahastra sang soi biraje | aap sada brahmachari ||3||
karma jaal katveke karan | sapanata thasab koi |
vedna jadi kachhu or | kupath padchya sab koi ||4||
sanskritme shukjie kahiya | prakrat santan vani |
lobh lahar aur vikhe vaasna | taame khenchatani ||5||
vis varaska purkha sunta | sol varaski naari |
kahat kabir bhali samjhai | bhulya chor katari ||6||_ (O saints, everyone is caught within the fold of the Vedas, and so the ill of [wrong] sentiment does not leave them; they say Hari once seated the gopi on his shoulder, pressing home such [a coarse notion of] devotion — whatever filth one hears, the mind conceives the same, and waves of poison arise. Talking knowledge upon knowledge, they drown all in the river of the three gunas; for the Brahma-jnani there is no true resting place — devotion cannot come by this way. The Complete Brahma who bore Mount Govardhan drank the forest-fire; that same one dwells amid sixteen thousand women, yet remains ever a Brahmachari. To cut the net of karma, everyone became entangled instead; being bound to the Vedas alone, everyone has fallen upon a wrong path. Shukji told it in Sanskrit, and the saints in the vernacular tongue — yet the waves of greed and poisonous desire keep pulling [such people] back and forth. Young men of twenty listen, and women of sixteen listen — says Kabir, though it was well explained, the deluded ones lost the very knife/key [of true understanding].)

Das Kabirji says: O saints! All the followers of the path of knowledge are trapped in the mass of the Vedas, and therefore, afflicted with this disease of [false] sentiment, they cannot hold their footing on the path of devotion. And these preachers of knowledge say that God once seated the gopi Radha upon His own shoulder — trying in this way to impress upon people this kind of obscene form of devotion — so that whatever filth is heard, the mind is tempted to do the same, and waves of sensual desire arise. These Brahma-jnanis, by repeatedly preaching this talk of knowledge — that Brahma alone dwells in all — impress upon people that they may indulge in sensory pleasures, and thereby drown everyone in the river of the three gunas' sensory pleasure. For such base, degraded so-called knowers of Brahma, there is no possibility whatsoever, anywhere in the world, of attaining supreme happiness. Because, believing that everything is of the nature of Brahma and behaving in this way in sensual desire, devotion to God cannot occur. If you call yourself "I am Brahma" and claim that you yourself are Brahma, then know that you will not be able to do what Shri Krishna, the Complete Brahma who held up Mount Govardhan, did — for he drank up the forest-fire. Such a capable, all-powerful Parbrahma, Shri Krishna, can remain seated amidst sixteen thousand women, entirely free of any disturbance [of passion]. In this way, even while dwelling among women, he remained ever the unbroken celibate (Brahmachari). To cut the net of karmic bondage, everyone used to listen to the character/deeds of Krishna, but true devotion was not obtained through the path of the Vedas, and instead everyone fell into a wrong, crooked path. Shukdev has described the divine play (leela) of Krishna in Sanskrit within the Bhagavat, and saints have sung the virtues of Krishna in the vernacular language — but because the waves of greed of self-interested people are directed towards sensory desire, they persist stubbornly in wishing to perform love-play like Krishna's. A young man of twenty years and a woman of sixteen years, hearing of such love-play, wrongly took it amiss — but just as, when a thief goes to commit a theft and forgets his main tool, the deed cannot be accomplished, in the same way, these so-called knowers of Brahma have missed the real, true mystery [of devotion], and therefore they will not attain a good end (sadgati).

In Nazre Nani's notebook no. 4, page 75, having written the above Asavari [hymn], he has recorded the following note: Bhagat Trikam Gordhan of Godana (Ghoda) village, in the book he himself wrote called "Santvani," on approximately page 431, has changed "brahmagyani" to "vakyagyani" (one knowledgeable in [mere] scriptural statements) — from which it is evident that he wanted to soften the blow that Kabir deals to those who claim to be knowers of Brahma. In the same way, in many other places, Trikam Gordhan (the bhagat of Ghoda village) has made changes in other kirtans as he wrote them down. In the samagam that he compiled, he has altered many words and other things, and has also written fabricated sakhis (couplets).

Followers of the path of knowledge cannot bear any opposition to knowledge. When Revered Yadunath Maharaj, in a katha (discourse), once recited two sakhis of Kalu Bhagat that expressed opposition to the path of knowledge, the followers of the knowledge-doctrine felt hurt in their minds. I too, knowingly and deliberately, recited those same sakhis in a katha at Siyabag; and so, the next day, Bhagat Bhagwan Bapu of Patra village, also known as Chetnadas, did not openly object, but sent a note [saying] that the meaning should be understood in the first line of Adhyaruji's 28 pads (hymns). The sakhis of Kalu Bhagat expressing opposition to the [false] path of knowledge are as follows, from Kathabodh Part 2, pages 140–141:

_unt gnan aap swarthi | oopar heeku khaay ||
sat shabd kalu kahai | koye nahi basaay ||1||_ (Camel-knowledge serves only its own self-interest, eating only what is above; the true word, says Kalu, gives no one entry.)

Kalu Bhagat says: knowledge [of this false kind] is something that acts only for its own self-interest. It is just like a camel that, standing tall outside the fence of a sugarcane field, eats only the leaves on top — it does not make any path by which anyone else could enter inside the fence; that is, it gives no opportunity for the ignorant to come to know anything.

_baad tod bhensa padi | peechhe marag hoy ||
parmarath kalu kahe | basaaye sab koy ||2||_ (The buffalo broke the fence and went in; behind her a path was made. Says Kalu: that is true benefit — by it, everyone finds a way in.)

Kalu Bhagat says: but the buffalo broke through the fence, making a gap, and went inside — and by this, it made a path by which small and large sheep and goats could also come in, thus performing an act of benefit for others. In just the same way, the "ignorant," like the buffalo, by breaking through the fence made of scriptures, Puranas, and Vedas, made a path of loving devotion (prem-bhakti) accessible to the unlettered.

In Krishnadasji's Parchari, it is said:

_kachhu na samjhe mero bhakt | so moku to pyaro lagta ||432||
mere santki sangat kije | aur baat hirde nahi dije ||432||_ ("My devotee who understands nothing else at all — such a one is very dear to Me. Keep the company of My saints, and give your heart to nothing else.")

"If My devotees know nothing at all about any other forms of worship besides the devoted worship of their chosen deity (ishtadev), such devotees are very dear to Me. Keep the company of saints who follow My teaching, and give no attention to any other matter besides that."

Those on the path of knowledge are worshippers of Omkar. But this Omkar is like a milestone. When one reaches the boundary of Vadodara, the milestone reads "Vadodara 0 miles," meaning that Vadodara has now arrived — but beyond that, what Vadodara itself is like, and how large it is, this milestone cannot say. In the same way, what loving devotion (prem-bhakti) truly is like becomes known through Ramkar (the sacred Ram-syllable). Thus, the path of [mere] knowledge halts at the level of the Vedas, Puranas, and scriptures, but it cannot reveal true devotion to God. Those who talk of knowledge aim to attain liberation through knowledge. In truth, everyone talks in this way, and great scholars or sadhu-saints say that knowledge should be attained — but the thing called "true knowledge" is not actually present in any such person. In the name of the Vedas, they push people toward ritualistic karma-kanda. Those who insist so strongly on the Vedas cling to the mere words of the Vedas and do not adopt practical understanding or the wisdom of discernment (vivek-buddhi); and clinging only to the [literal] words, these "knowers of Brahma" fall into misconduct. In truth, they do not know what real knowledge is, or what it should be like.

One person, who had become obsessed and maddened in pursuit of knowledge, went to Kabir and asked: "Tell me, what are the limits of knowledge? In this constant searching and searching for knowledge, I have become utterly bewildered." Then Kabirji said:

_padhneki had samaj hai | samajki had gnan ||
gnanki had harinaam hai | eh siddhant dar aan ||_ (The limit of reading/study is understanding; the limit of understanding is knowledge; the limit of knowledge is the Name of God — hold this settled truth firmly within.)

Das Kabirji says: the limit of reading/studying extends up to the point of understanding, and the limit of understanding extends up to knowledge/awareness, and the limit of knowledge/awareness extends up to the Name of God — hold this settled conclusion within your heart.

_gnanika to guru hu | agnanika daas ||
jahan jahan dekhu dhingadhingi | dantu pakadu dhaas ||_ (To the man of knowledge I am the guru; to the man without knowledge I am a servant. Wherever I see quarrelsome commotion, I hold my teeth and bow away from it.)

Das Kabirji says: if you call yourself a man of knowledge, then I am the supreme guru who gives knowledge to men of knowledge. And if you do not call yourself a man of knowledge — that is, if you show humility — then I will become your servant, your humble, unassuming servant who accepts you. And wherever I see the turmoil of quarrelsome argument and dispute, there I will simply bow to them from a distance; I will not enter into debate with them.

_kabir gnani gnata bahu mile | kavi pandit anek ||
raam rata aru drijita | te koti madhye ek ||65||_ (Kabir says: those who know knowledge, who speak of it, are found in plenty, and so are poets and pandits in great numbers; but one absorbed in love for Ram, master of his senses — such a one is rare, one in a crore.)

Das Kabirji says: those who know knowledge and talk about knowledge are found in great numbers, and poets, bards, and pandits are found in many numbers too. But one who is full of love in devotion to Ram, and who has gained mastery over the senses — such a one is found only rarely, one among crores.

_kabir gnan kathi ganda bhaya | laade bail pachaas ||
man daska pota liya | nahi pahechanki aas ||38||_ (Kabir says: talking knowledge upon knowledge, they have gone mad, loading fifty bullock-carts [of scriptures]; though they have taken up ten maunds of dust-wiping [labour], there remains no hope of true recognition.)

Das Kabirji says: by talking of knowledge again and again, they have become mad and utterly bewildered, and they load up as much as fifty cartloads of worthless books/pedantry [to carry around]; and even after taking on as much as ten maunds' worth of effort in "cleansing" [scholarly labor], still there remains no hope of arriving at true understanding.

Gnani (the man of knowledge) — Gnan (knowledge) is nothing but a collection of information. Sant (the saint) — to apply that information in a known situation is understanding. Guru — application: to apply that information in an unknown situation is "explication" (in Gujarati: vikasavu, ughadu karvu — to develop, to bring out into the open). Sadguru — skill (kaushalya): to create new information for any situation, whether known or unknown — a "blueprint" (roop-rekha): able to draw up the design, able to bring about a wholly new creation.

_gnan graho kabirka | aur gnan sab jhooth ||
jehi gnanme hari basai | bharle taki mooth ||2||_ (Take up only Kabir's knowledge; all other knowledge is false. Grasp firmly that knowledge within which Hari himself dwells.)

Nana Parekh says: accept only the teaching of knowledge given by Kabirji — all other teachings of knowledge are false. So gather up and hold on to that teaching of Kabirji's, in which the possibility of attaining God is present.

_gnan kathe so bavara | mukti mage so moodh ||
prem bhakti bin jivana | jamku phansi praudh ||63||_ (One who [merely] discourses on knowledge is deranged; one who begs for liberation is a fool. Without loving devotion, O Jivana, a heavy noose from Yama's [death's] hand awaits.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: those who, like the Sanaka brothers and others, keep engaging in discussion — analysis, reflection, imagination, and debate — in pursuit of Brahma-jnana, self-knowledge, and scholarship, are bewildered and confounded. And those who plead and beg to attain liberation are foolish — because even if one attains such knowledge or liberation without loving devotion (prem-bhakti), Yamraj (the god of death) will certainly mete out severe punishment.

_gnan gnan sabko kahai | gnan na chihne koi ||
je gnane girdhar mile | gnan kahave soi ||_ (Everyone keeps saying "knowledge, knowledge," yet no one truly recognizes what knowledge is. Only that knowledge by which Girdhar [Krishna] is attained deserves to be called knowledge.)

Nana Parekh says: everyone keeps talking about all kinds of knowledge — self-knowledge, Brahma-knowledge, philosophical knowledge, and so on. But no one truly explains what real knowledge actually is. Only that teaching by which God is attained can rightly be called true knowledge-teaching.

"Gnanam bharah kriyam vina" — knowledge without action is nothing but a burden upon the head. "Sa vidya ya vimuktaye" — that alone is true learning which grants us liberation.

_kabir jeta ghat teta mata | ghat ghat aur subhaav ||
ja ghat haar na jit hai | ta ghat brahma samaay ||_ (Kabir says: as many bodies as there are, so many are the differing opinions — every body has its own disposition. But in that body where there is neither defeat nor victory, there Brahma is contained.)

Das Kabirji says: in the world, however many bodies there are, that many differing opinions and doctrines exist. But in that body where there is no joy or sorrow, no defeat or victory, no "I"-ness (ego) — there the essence of the Supreme Soul is contained.

Sanakadi (The Sanaka Brothers)

_kapil munike krodhke | maare sagarke poot ||
sanakadikne krodh kari | rakshas kiye hari doot ||_ (By the anger of Kapil Muni, King Sagar's sons were killed; by their anger, the Sanaka brothers turned Hari's own doorkeepers into demons.)

Just as, because of Kapil Muni's anger, King Sagar's sixty thousand sons died, in that same way, the Sanaka brothers, through their anger, cursed God's own doorkeeper-messengers Jaya and Vijaya to become demons (rakshasas).

In the Samagam, the ten avatars have been called a shahukar chor (a respectable thief). Now, there are in fact twenty-four avatars, among which the Sanaka brothers are counted as God's first avatar. So neither the ten avatars nor the twenty-four avatars are accepted [as the complete literal truth]; therefore the Samagam has spoken of the Sanaka brothers as one of the seven shahukar chors.

_aham mite nahi jivana | sanakadikse sadh ||
brahmadik rachpach mue | aham badi ipadh ||3||_ (Even in a saint like the Sanaka brothers, O Jivana, ego does not depart. Brahma and others too remained engrossed in it and perished — ego is a great affliction.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says: even the ego of great siddhas (perfected ones) such as the Sanaka brothers could not be erased; and likewise, Brahma and others too remained absorbed and engrossed in it, and were defeated and perished in it. Therefore ego (ahankar) is a great affliction, a great calamity.

These mind-born sons of Brahmaji wandered everywhere at will, naked and free, remaining permanently at the age of five years. Once they went to Brahmaji and began to ask: "We have seen all fourteen worlds, but we have not found eternal peace. We keep lust and anger under our control; maya does not even come near us — but show us a realm where there is not the slightest trace of sorrow."

Brahmaji saw that sprouts of pride had arisen in these children. These ones did indeed possess knowledge — they had come to have more or less full knowledge of Shabda-Brahma (the Word-Brahma) and Parabrahma — but they had not developed a taste for devotion (bhakti), and without devotion, ego is never destroyed. [Brahma thought:] "Even if I try to explain this to them, they will not accept it — for they carry the pride that their own father is engrossed in worldly entanglement, that Brahmaji is lustful, having become infatuated with his own daughter Saraswati, while they think, 'we, on the other hand, have conquered lust' — this was their pride." A father must sometimes send his own son elsewhere to be taught, and there was no one who could teach them this lesson except the Lord of Vaikuntha. So Brahma said to them: "The fourteen worlds are all places from which one returns [i.e., subject to rebirth]. But have you ever seen Vaikuntha?" Then they replied, "That we have not seen." Brahma said: "If you have not seen Vaikuntha, then you have seen nothing at all."

Describing Vaikuntha, Brahma said that in that realm there is a forest named "Naishreyasa" (the one useful for [attaining] liberation), which appears to be like kaivalya-mukti (absolute, final liberation) itself. Moreover, Shri Hari adorns his own divine form with tulsi (holy basil), and holds tulsi in the highest regard.

Moreover, at the beginning of creation, Brahmaji performed austerities (tapasya) with the wish to bring the various worlds into being; and, pleased by that austerity, God — taking on the name-prefix "San," meaning [connected to] austerity — took avatar in the forms of Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan, and Sanatkumar. What were these Sanaka brothers like? They had accomplished the khechari mudra (a yogic seal) and, through the adho-mudra (an inverted posture), drank the nectar of immortality (amrit), thereby making their perishable bodies imperishable — and by their very nature they remain always at the age of twelve years.

By their own yogic power, the Sanaka brothers set out to enter Vaikuntha; they passed through six gateways, but at the seventh gate Jaya and Vijaya stopped them. Filled with anger, they cursed these doorkeepers to be born in the race of demons (rakshasas). Thus the Sanaka brothers were not able to conquer their own pride/ego. By the power of their spiritual practice and learning, they were able to keep only their bodies at the age of five years, but their intellect was not innocent like that of true children — they were child-like only in outward appearance. In truth, since they did not have a child's innocent intellect, they may be called pretenders (dhongi/hypocrites). Their doubt was not resolved by Brahma. Then God, taking the form of the Hansavatar (the Swan-avatar), gave them knowledge. But that knowledge proved of no use when anger arose in them — so knowledge alone cannot restrain pride/ego; rather, it can instead make one more proud. By taking the Hansavatar, God resolved the doubt of the Sanaka brothers. The hans (swan) is a being with the quality of separating milk from water. Therefore, the task of separating out the element of maya from the mixture of maya and Brahma, and revealing the true essence of Brahma, is like the work of a swan. For this reason, Jivanji Maharaj, in order to resolve this confusion between the great Brahma and maya, has given this teaching in the Samagam: he has instructed that one should live in this great world (samsar) while remaining untouched by maya, and practice devotion.

Why devotion to Vishnu alone? Adhyaruji states, in the Harsh Bhavan (chapter):

_sur nar munijan gahi gaya re | samrath vishnu aadhar ||
brahma vishnu maheshwar re | na lahe taro paar re ||3||_ (Gods, humans, and sages too have taken hold of the support of the mighty Vishnu and crossed over; even Brahma, Vishnu, and Maheshwar cannot fathom your far shore.)

Gods, humans, and sages too have taken refuge in the powerful support of Maha-Vishnu, the Parbrahma, and have thereby crossed over [the ocean of worldly existence]; and even the three great gods — Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva — are not able to fathom your divine play (leela).

_je man hari samaran nahi re | je mukh nahi hari naam ||
vishnu bhakti antar nahi re | na lahe taro paar re ||3||_ (Those whose mind holds no remembrance of Hari, whose mouth carries not the Name of Hari, in whose heart is no devotion to Vishnu — such ones cannot cross to your far shore.)

Those in whose minds no wish even arises to perform devotion to God or to remember Him, and from whose mouths even the Name of God is not taken, and within whose hearts there is not even the sentiment of devotion to Vishnu — such people, in the end, find their place in hell.

Shiva devotees, under the name of Mahashiva, claim the essence of Parbrahma [for Shiva]. But Shaiva worship is based on Omkar, while Vishnu worship is based on Ramkar (the Ram-syllable). Shiva devotees also accept devotion to the Mother [Goddess], and in the name of the Mother Goddess, goats are sacrificed/slaughtered — and even the great Shankaracharyas of today's modern age raise no objection to this. Is this not exactly equivalent to the practice of qurbani (animal sacrifice) followed in the Muslim community? Is such sacrifice, done in this way, really proper? Therefore, devotion to Vishnu is pure, unstained loving devotion. Adhyaruji's statement is correct in this way: that people who practice devotion wrongly, without devotion to Vishnu, engage in conduct fit only for going directly to hell — and so they will have to suffer hell.

_bhai re dui jagdish kahan te aaye | kahu kaune bharmaya |
allah ram karima keshav | hari hazrat naam gharaya ||_ ("O brother, from where have two Lords of the Universe come? Tell me, who has deluded you into this? Allah, Ram, Karim, Keshav, Hari, Hazrat — these are but names given to the one.")

"O brother, from where have two Lords of the Universe (Jagdish) come? Tell me, who has deluded you into this? Allah, Ram, Karim, Keshav, Hari, Hazrat — these are merely different names; you yourself say it is, in truth, one alone." This much is fine — but the polytheistic belief in 33 crore gods and so on has gone too far. In truth, the ruler and controller of the world is the one and only Parbrahma, the Supreme Soul — but the various doctrine-holders have created confusion and delusion about this.

(Raga Sindhudo)

_harinaam vina nar sootki re | mahapataki re tene aabhadvano adhikar nahi |
evi ved purane vani kahi ||tek||
hari naam vina narke jaaye | jam traas dei tene kanthe saahe ||
jire mai to khat darshna ghapam joya | hari naam vina divas te sakhe khoya ||
sadhana sadhtaa je re mohya | janam janam manav vagoya ||1||
jire sur muni gandharva rishi ja kahave | sapane harinaam na tehaj paave ||
ghare soonya dhyaan ghat ghat bataave | e mugati maarag kyam bhagati aave ||2||
jire shuk sanakadik rahe je bhamta | tene sapne na jaanya ruda ram ramta ||
amo haridarsani manma ehaj mamta | te shri damodarrayne nav gamta ||3||
jire meru sahit mahi shesh jaaye | viraj angana mali jas sujas gaaye ||
taha krishna kreeda kare raas mahe | taha narsaiyo charanni ren naahye ||4||_ (Without devotion to Hari's Name, a man remains unclean, a great sinner with no right even to be touched — so declare the very words of Veda and Purana. Without Hari's Name, one goes to hell, where Yama's men seize him by the throat in torment. I have examined the six schools of philosophy, but without Hari's Name my days were spent to no purpose; those absorbed in [mere] spiritual disciplines have squandered human birth, life after life. Those called gods, sages, gandharvas, and rishis never once obtain Hari's Name even in a dream; they show the void, [pointing to] meditation on the formless present in every body — how then can devotion arise through this path of liberation-seeking? Shukdev and the Sanaka brothers keep wandering thus, never knowing even in dream the beautiful, ever-sporting Ram; but in the minds of us who long for Hari's vision this same longing dwells — and to Shri Damodar Ray's devotees, such people are not pleasing. Go from Mount Meru all the way to Sheshnag beneath the earth, and you will find the gopis gathered, singing His glory and praise, where Krishna sports in the raas dance, and where Narsaiyo [Narsinh Mehta] bathes in the dust of His feet.)

Without devotion to the Name of God, a person is unclean/defiled, is a great sinner — and there is no exemption for anyone from this rule; so declare the very words of the Vedas. Without the Name of God, a person falls into hell, where the servants of Yama (death) seize him by the throat and inflict severe torment upon him. I have examined the four principles/rules laid down by the six schools of philosophy (khat-darshan), but since they lack devotion to the Name of God, all the time spent practicing their disciplines has been wasted uselessly. Those who have become attached to accomplishing [various] spiritual practices (sadhanas) have ruined their human birth, life after life. Those who call themselves gods, sages, gandharvas, rishis, and so on — even in their dreams, they never once get to take the Name of God. Those who meditate on the formless and say that the essence of God resides in every single body — how can they attain the path of devotion through the path of [mere] liberation-seeking? Shukdev and the Sanaka brothers keep wandering about in this way, but even in their dreams they never come to know the beautiful, all-pervading Ram as He truly is. But people like us keep, in our minds, a deep longing for the vision (darshan) of God — and to us, the devotees of Shri Damodar Ray [Krishna], such people are not pleasing. If you go and look, from Mount Meru all the way down to Sheshnag in the netherworld, you will find that the gopis of Vraj and others all gather together and sing bhajans and kirtans of God — and it is in that very atmosphere that Lord Krishna sports in the raas dance. It is in such devotion that Narsinh Mehta finds joy and delight, in the shelter of God.

Because the Sanaka brothers were spiritually corrupt without devotion, they, under the pretext of Jaya and Vijaya's curse, took three births as devotees and thereby obtained devotion. First they became a devotee as Prahlad; then they became a devotee as Vibhishan; and then, becoming a devotee as Bhishma, they learned the lesson of devotion. Narsinh Mehta, along with many other saints, has condemned these Sanaka brothers for their shortcoming. Jivanji, in plain, clear words, has openly declared them a shahukar chor (respectable thief); and Narsinh Mehta, too, in the same way as Jivanji, has regarded both the [claim of God dwelling formlessly in "every body," urged by knowledge-seekers,] and the Sanaka brothers as reprehensible.

Gayaldas, writing about prem-bhakti (loving devotion) in his Doomela Sorathas, in the 15th Soratha, mentions the Sanaka brothers and writes:

_e jog vairagko desh | te sanakadiksu jai male ||
jaanha karam dharmki aash | taame sab jiv aathale ||15||_ (That is the land of yoga and renunciation, where one goes and meets the Sanaka brothers — but where hope still clings to ritual and duty, there every soul stumbles and is lost.)

Such pretenders/impostors dwell in the very birthplace of the path of yoga. They cling to the mode of worship set forth by the Sanaka-brother sages, in which — following the path of ritual karma-kanda, or Vedic religion, and sakama-bhakti (devotion performed for the sake of reward) — hope and expectation of fruit/result remains, through the path of knowledge, the path of action, or the path of yoga. In this, all these souls become entangled/trapped.

_teen lok chori bhai | sahka sarbas leenh ||
bina moodka chokha | para na kahu cheenh ||125||_ (The headless one has plundered all three worlds and taken away everyone's all — this thief without a head, no one at all recognizes him.)

The headless thief — the formless Brahma — is not recognized by anyone. He committed theft across all three worlds and stole away everything. The devotees of the Goddess with the severed head — that power/Shakti — cannot be recognized either. This headless one, everyone dissolves and merges into the essence of Omkar. This thief has stolen away everyone's knowledge, and has cast everyone into the womb [i.e., into the cycle of rebirth]. The Goddess Chhinnamastaka is [identified with] Durga Devi; this has been described in the Bhagavad Gomandal (encyclopedic dictionary). Her photograph, too, appears in Kalyan, year 81, issue 3, in the section on the ten Mahavidyas, at the back.

_chaar chor chori chale | pagu panhi utaar ||
charo dar dhuni hani | pandit karahu vichaar ||127||_ (Four thieves set out to steal, having removed the sandals from their feet; they struck at all four doors — reflect on this, O pandit.)

The four Vedas, as four thieves, set out to plunder the soul's [true] wealth. But no one at all realized that this thief was committing theft within our very own body. All four persons of the four ashramas [stages of life] took off the sandals that protect their feet — that is, their devotion — and walked on after the ritual karma-kanda of the Vedas.

_shahu chor cheenhai nahi | andha matika heen ||
parakh bina vinaash hai | karu vichaar ho bheen ||156||_ (One who cannot tell the honest merchant from the thief is blind and lacking in understanding; without discernment lies ruin — reflect on this and understand aright.)

Worldly souls are blind, because they cannot tell apart the true guru — the honest merchant (shah) in the form of the true Self — from the deceiving thief; and so they are being plundered by keeping company with thieves. Without the true guru as the honest merchant, and by remaining in the company of thieves in the form of the Vedas, scriptures, Puranas, minor deities, and false "Brahma-gurus," the soul has been destroyed. Therefore, reflect carefully, and abandon such false gurus.

_shahu to bho chokha | choran te bho jujja ||
tab jaanaigo jiyara | maar pahaigo tujja ||148||_ (At first the merchant remained pure, [then] he too became embroiled with the thieves; only when the blow falls, O soul, will you understand.)

At first the honest merchant (shah) remained pure and untouched; but Brahma-maya (the delusive mind) steals him, and in this way he too became a thief — that is, by giving this teaching, the mind-thief stole away the soul's knowledge of the true Master, and began to say: "You yourself are Brahma; why should you worship the Primordial Power (Adi-Shakti)? The mind alone is the cause of both bondage and liberation." In this way, a battle took place with the guru-thief, and it was said to the soul: "When Ram's blow falls upon you, then you will understand that your true protector was made to be forgotten — that by calling yourself Brahma, you were made to give up devotion — only then will you understand."
